title: feat(types): the four page: containers take their child list in properties.children, and objectql.zod.ts shares propsBag (objectui#10872, batch 6)
body:
Part of #10872
Clause-②: yes

**objectui#10872 batch 6: the four `page:` containers take their child list in `properties.children`.** `page:card`, `page:section`, `page:footer` and `page:sidebar` now refuse a node-level `children` by name, and restate `body` with the same message. The message's first sentence names `properties.children`, the member each block's `@objectstack/spec` row declares. Also in this PR, with no behaviour change: `objectql.zod.ts`'s two public-block arms import the one `propsBag` helper instead of keeping a byte copy of it.

The card stays open. `record:line_items` (no spec row yet) and the rest of the flat-props / envelope-key batch remain, as the claim and release `5909279008` list them.

## The ruling this executes, and the premises it rests on

The seat applied triage's `action:*` answer (`5906817482`: "The `properties` bag is the contract", "B is not taken … a second dialect") to this branch. The ruling holds only on premises 1–4 of the order, so each was measured before the first edit to the four arms. All four hold for all four containers.

| # | premise | reading (objectui `origin/main` `cfc9b6db98`, installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0) | holds |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | the installed spec refuses a node-level `children` on all four | `PageComponentSchema.safeParse({ type, children: [node] })`: `unrecognized_keys` with keys `["children"]` on each of the four. The message reads "Unrecognized key(s) on this page component: `children`. Before ADR-0089 D3a these were dropped silently…". `{ type, properties: { children } }` and a bare `{ type }` both pass. Control: `page:tabs`, `page:header` and `record:details` give the same refusal, so the instrument is live. | yes, 4 of 4 |
| 2 | each row declares `children` inside `properties` | `ComponentPropsMap['page:card']` is `PageCardProps`, with keys `title`, `bordered`, `actions`, `children`, `body`, `footer`, `aria`. `actions` and `body` are `[REMOVED]` tombstones, and `body`'s text says "Rename the key to `children`". The other three rows are all `PageContainerProps` (identity checked), whose one key is `children`. Every `children` is `z.array(z.unknown())` and optional, and each row parses `{ children: [node] }`. | yes, 4 of 4 |
| 3 | a spec-shaped node renders its children through objectui today | This was a one-off runtime probe, never committed, through the real `SchemaRenderer`, `ActionProvider`, `I18nProvider` and the `@object-ui/components` registry (happy-dom). Each container got two `element:text` markers in `properties.children`. **All four rendered both markers, in order, and the DOM was byte-identical to the node-level spelling.** The roots were `div.rounded-lg.border.bg-card` (card), `section.space-y-4`, the separator-led footer and `aside.flex.flex-col.gap-4`. Control: with no children, the render had 0 markers. The mechanism is `SchemaRenderer`'s `properties` hoist, which copies every bag key except `type` / `id` onto the node the renderer reads. | yes, 4 of 4 |
| 4 | no objectui or objectstack writer emits a node-level `children` on the four | Census: `node scripts/body-dialect-census.mjs --keys page:card,page:section,page:footer,page:sidebar,page:tabs,page:accordion,grid,flex,card --json`. **objectui** (9440 files): 7 nodes of the four types carry a node-level `children`, all in the `test` bucket (six `page:section` and one `page:card`, in app-shell render tests). There are 0 in `apps` / `examples` / `content/docs` / `skills` / `packages/*/src`. Lit control: `card` has 88 node-level `children` in `example-app` and `flex` has 251. **objectstack** (`origin/main` `72f8c38201`, `apps` / `examples` / `packages` / `content` archived into the scratchpad, 8379 files): 109 nodes of the four types (83 `page:card`, 20 `page:section`, 1 `page:footer`, 5 `page:sidebar`), and **0** carry a node-level `children`. Lit control: `flex` has 2. The showcase's own `my-work` page writes `page:card` with `properties.children`, and the spec lint's `page-walk` says "`PageComponentSchema` is `.strict()`, so a component carries no `children` key of its own". **Writers read directly:** the page designer's canvas addresses `properties.children` for `page:card` and `page:section` (`childGroups` in `PageBlockCanvas`), and for any block that already carries that array. The inspector writes every prop into `properties` (`patchProp`). The default page synthesizer (`buildDefaultPageSchema`'s `componentNode`) emits `{ type, properties }` and none of the four types. | yes, 4 of 4 |
| 5 | `objectBlockPropsBag` is a byte copy of `propsBag` | With only the function name normalised, the two 8-line bodies have the same md5 (`d7a54fe8…`) and `diff` exits 0. Folded: `propsBag` is exported from `public-blocks.zod.ts` and `objectql.zod.ts` imports it. There is no third copy, and the barrel still does not re-export it. | yes |
| 6 | `NAMESPACED_REFUSED_AT_TYPE` does not move | The diff of the ratchet file against the base is empty, and `registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts` is green in the sweep below. | yes |

## What changed

- `packages/types/src/zod/public-blocks.zod.ts`
  - Each of the four arms declares `children` and `body` as `retirementTombstone` members. Both are fed ONE string from a new local composer, `pageContainerChildListGuidance(type, row)`. This is the objectui#9256 construct with a different message: these blocks do render their child list, so the neither-channel text would be false for them. The first sentence names `properties.children`, the row (`PageCardProps` / `PageContainerProps`) and the node to write. The message also says the spec refuses the node-level spelling, and that the hoist makes the move a no-op at render time.
  - `propsBag` is exported, and its docblock says it is the one copy, internal, and not re-exported from `index.zod.ts`.
  - The module docblock's "content channels" section gains a paragraph for the four containers. The flat-key paragraph no longer says a flat `body` on the containers is refused by the base's objectui#6771 retirement, "whose `children` remedy they do render": this diff makes that false.
- `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`: the `objectBlockPropsBag` copy is deleted, and `object-metric` and `object-master-detail-form` build `properties` with the imported `propsBag`.
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/container-children-channel-10872.test.ts` (new, 102 tests), in four groups:
  - (a) Refusal, on both faces. `invalid_type` at the key's own path, and a first sentence naming `properties.children`, the block, the row and the node to write. Neither the neither-channel text nor the "Did you mean `body` → `children`?" remedy appears. One string feeds `.describe()` and the issue message, every value is refused, and both keys are members.
  - (b) Positive controls, on both faces. `properties.children` parses, the bare node parses, the bag spelling parses nested in a `page` while the node-level spelling is refused there at `children.0.children`, and `page:card`'s full row (`title`, `bordered`, `children`, `footer`) parses.
  - (c) The installed spec. It refuses the node-level spelling and passes the bag spelling, and each row still declares `children`, so the remedy names a real member.
  - (d) The fold. Both `objectql.zod.ts` arms' `properties` description is word-for-word the helper's text, from the same composer as the `public-blocks.zod.ts` arms.
- `.changeset/10872-container-children-channel.md`: `'@object-ui/types': minor`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, see below.

## Surface beyond the order's file list, each forced by this diff and declared

- `content-channel-public-blocks-9256.test.ts`: its "CONTROL — `%s` renders the node's child list, so it still takes `children`" rows asserted that the four ACCEPT a node-level `children`, which is the exact behaviour this batch narrows. The control keeps its purpose, which is to show that a reader keeps its channel. It now asserts `properties.children` parses on the arm and on `AnyComponentSchema`, and that the node-level refusal is not the neither-channel text. Text of the other rows is untouched.
- `record-alert-flat-body-remedy-10872.test.ts`: its "CONTROL arm — `page:card` … keeps `BaseSchema`'s objectui#6771 refusal" asserted the old `body` message on `page:card`, which this batch restates. The control moves to `card`, which reads the node-level `children` and keeps the objectui#6771 remedy. It asserts the same three facts, and a comment records the move.
- `packages/types/src/zod/README.md`: one sentence. "Every arm except the four `page:` containers … refuses `children` and `body`" would now misdescribe the four, so it gains a sentence saying they refuse both with a message naming `properties.children`. This follows AGENTS.md #2, and batch 5's README hunk was ratified on the same ground.
- `.changeset/10872-public-block-zod-arms.md` (pending, batch 1): a dated note only, with the frontmatter untouched. Its flat-props bullet says `children` on the four is "judged against the base's own types", and that `body` on `page:card` is refused "by the base's objectui#6771 retirement". Neither describes the release as a whole any more. This is the dated-note precedent of batches 2–4 on that same file.
- `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: the four `EXCLUSIONS` reason strings name the new members (text only, the order's allowance).

## Changeset: `minor`, and why

- The accept set narrows against `main` on four exported arms: a node-level `children` is refused where it parsed. Hence `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.
- The arm is `minor`, on the objectui#9256 / batch-5 precedent. This repo forbids `major` in any changeset (one `fixed` group) and spells a narrowing as `minor` with an explicit note.
- It is not breaking against the last release. The published `@object-ui/types` 17.6.0 (npm `latest`, 2026-08-24) carries no public-block arm: its dist has 0 hits for `PageCardBlockSchema` / `PageSectionBlockSchema` / `PublicBlockComponentSchema`, against 1 each for the controls `CardSchema` / `FlexSchema`. Its `safeValidateSchema` answers `invalid_union` for `{ type: 'page:section' }`, with or without children and with a bag, and for `page:footer` / `page:sidebar`, while the control `{ type: 'card', children: [...] }` passes. So across the release the accept set only widens.

None touches a file of this diff. `git merge-tree` was clean, `main` was merged in (merge, no rebase), and the matrix above was rerun on the merge. The seat named an in-flight branch for objectui#9547 that edits `objectql.zod.ts` (its `onNavigate` region) and `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` (its own rows). This diff's hunks there are the helper region and the four container rows only.

## Acceptance notes (not filed; for the seat)

1. **The bag's nested nodes are not judged by objectui's validator.** This predates the batch, and the batch makes the bag the only channel on these four. The spec rows type `children` (and `page:tabs` / `page:accordion` `items[].children`) as `z.array(z.unknown())`. So `{ type: 'page:section', properties: { children: [{ type: 'no-such-type-xyz' }] } }` parses green on both faces, and so does a malformed `element:text` there. The same child written at node level was refused (`invalid_union` at `children`). The spec's lint walks those bag arrays by hand (`page-walk`), so `os validate` still judges them. What this batch moves is only which spelling is accepted, not whether nested content is judged by the publish gate. The pre-existing gap belongs in its own card. Dedupe words: `properties.children nested node not validated` · `bag slot children z.array(z.unknown()) objectui validate` · `items[].children unjudged safeValidateSchema`.
2. **The parser tier still accepts the node-level spelling.** `@object-ui/sdui-parser`'s `BASE_PROPS` lists `children`, and `isContainer` authorises it on the four, so the manifest tier and the VS Code validator pass a node-level `children` that both zod faces now refuse. This is batch 3's `record:alert` pattern. The carrier is this card's flat-props / envelope-key batch, whose order names both tiers. ⛔ Not touched here: the order excludes `packages/sdui-parser` and `packages/vscode-extension`.
3. **A committed runtime pin for premise 3 is not in this PR.** Zone 3 suggested one. It would need `@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/components` in a DOM project, but `@object-ui/types` imports no renderer and its tests run in the `unit` (node) project. Its home would be `packages/components/src/__tests__/`, which is outside the claimed surface. The probe's readings are in premise 3 above. If the seat wants it pinned, a follow-up with that surface is a small test.
4. `skills/objectui/guides/page-builder.md` says the three thin containers "render a `section`, `footer` and `aside` around their `children`". That is prose, true at runtime, and names no node spelling. It is governed, so it is only noted here.
